blocks.text:
Wulaia Bay / Cape Horn. Before dawn, the ship passes through the Murray Channel between Navarino and Hoste islands to anchor in historic Wulaia Bay, once a major settlement of the Yámana people, described by Charles Darwin and drawn by Captain FitzRoy during the voyage of HMS Beagle in the 1830s. Visit the museum in the old radio station, on the history of the Yámana people and European missionaries, then choose one of three trails through Magellanic forest of lenga, coigüe, canelo and ferns to a viewpoint over the bay. Before leaving, drop a postcard in the wooden mailbox, to be delivered by hand by future travellers.

In the afternoon, cross Nassau Bay to Cape Horn National Park. Weather permitting, land on the windswept island of Cape Horn, discovered in 1616 by a Dutch expedition and named after the town of Hoorn: a sheer 425-metre rock towering over the Drake Passage. For centuries, until the Panama Canal opened, rounding the Horn was the main sea route between the Atlantic and the Pacific, and the cape was called the “End of the World”. Declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2005, the island has a Chilean Navy lighthouse, home to a keeper and family, the tiny Stella Maris chapel and a modern Cape Horn monument.
